steps.intent: Our primary objective is to renew the mandate of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission for another 12 months to maintain international momentum and reinforce the Haitian National Police against armed gangs ahead of planned elections. The main points of friction during negotiations will center on funding mechanisms and any language referencing the potential transition of the MSS mission into a formal UN peacekeeping operation, which China and the Russian Federation strongly resist. To secure adoption without risking a veto, the draft focuses on extending the existing Chapter VII authorization, emphasizing voluntary contributions and accountability while keeping future options under active Council consideration.

messages.Algeria: Algeria welcomes this draft resolution extending the mandate of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission and commends the leadership of Kenya, participating personnel, and CARICOM partners. We stress that addressing the security crisis requires not only sustained and predictable financing for the MSS mission, but also a strictly enforced arms embargo to choke off illicit weapons flows fueling gang violence. We also reaffirm that any sustainable solution must remain strictly Haitian-led and Haitian-owned, addressing the socioeconomic root causes of instability.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of the MSS mission's mandate to assist the Haitian National Police in curbing gang violence. However, security assistance alone cannot solve Haiti's deep-seated crisis; steming the flow of illicit weapons into Haiti is paramount, and the draft must adequately reflect the vital role of the arms embargo. Furthermore, discussions on the future footprint or financing modalities of international security assistance must remain cautious, grounded in consensus, and respect the voluntary framework established for the MSS mission.
messages.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports the renewal of the authorization for the Multinational Security Support mission and appreciates the penholders' timely initiative. To ensure the mission's credibility and long-term effectiveness, we wish to reinforce language regarding human rights compliance, accountability, and the protection of vulnerable groups, particularly women and children. We stand ready to work constructively with the co-sponsors towards the swift adoption of this text.
messages.France: France commends the co-penholders for their swift work and fully supports extending the mandate of the Multinational Security Support mission for twelve months. To maximize operational effectiveness and build trust with the local population, we believe the text should highlight the importance of linguistic capabilities in French and Haitian Creole for deployed personnel. We also remain convinced that the Council must continue to explore more predictable and sustainable financing modalities for international security assistance in Haiti.
messages.Greece: Greece strongly supports the renewal of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission's mandate and commends the co-penholders, the United States and Panama, for their leadership, as well as Kenya and contributing nations for their dedication on the ground. We believe strengthening the text with explicit references to the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse and child protection will further reinforce the mission's credibility and adherence to international human rights standards. Greece stands ready to support the swift adoption of this critical resolution.
messages.Guyana: Guyana warmly thanks the United States and Panama for circulating this draft extending the MSS mission's vital mandate. As a fellow CARICOM nation, Guyana underscores the indispensable role of regional personnel and CARICOM's ongoing political facilitation efforts, which should be explicitly recognized in the text. Furthermore, given the acute funding constraints hindering the mission's full deployment, we must convey a much stronger call for urgent, predictable, and sustainable resources.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the proposed renewal of the authorization for the Multinational Security Support mission to assist Haiti in addressing severe gang violence and restoring public security. We believe the resolution should explicitly highlight the need to curb the illicit trafficking of firearms that fuels these criminal groups, as well as the importance of humanitarian assistance alongside security measures. We look forward to working constructively with the penholders towards a consensual adoption.
messages.Panama: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution, Panama fully supports the text and underscores the critical importance of extending the authorization of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission to help stabilize Haiti. Sustained international security assistance, adequate and predictable financing, and close coordination with the Haitian National Police and BINUH are vital to restoring security and enabling a viable political transition toward free and fair elections. We urge all Council members to support this draft and ensure the swift and unified renewal of the MSS mission's mandate.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea strongly supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission for an additional twelve months. We commend the United States and Panama for their leadership and appreciate the draft's clear emphasis on enhancing Haitian National Police capacity and securing sustainable support for the mission. Korea remains committed to supporting the MSS mission and the Haitian people, and we stand ready to support the swift adoption of this text.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports extending the mandate of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission in Haiti unchanged, acknowledging the ongoing efforts of Kenya and other contributing States. However, we firmly believe it is premature to prejudge any transformation of the mission into a UN peacekeeping operation, and the text must not serve as a backdoor for such initiatives. Crucially, the resolution must address the root driver of gang violence by demanding concrete action to halt the illicit influx of weapons and ammunition flooding into Haiti.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone, aligned with the A3+ and our regional partners, fully supports the renewal of the MSS mission's authorization and commends Kenya and contributing nations for their leadership. However, the current voluntary funding model is unsustainable and jeopardizes the mission's operational success on the ground. We urge the penholders to reflect the urgent need for predictable and sustainable financing, as well as to formally address the Haitian authorities' request regarding a transition towards a UN peacekeeping operation.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia strongly supports the extension of the MSS mission's mandate and thanks the United States and Panama for circulating this timely draft. In line with our core priorities, we would like to see explicit references to child protection, the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, and strict adherence to international humanitarian and human rights law. We look forward to constructive negotiations and stand ready to vote in favour of the text.
messages.Somalia: Somalia strongly supports the renewal of the MSS mission mandate and commends the fraternal leadership and sacrifice of Kenya and other contributing nations in assisting Haiti. To ensure the mission's operational success on the ground, the international community must provide adequate, predictable, and sustainable financing and logistical support. We also emphasize the necessity of curbing the illicit flow of weapons and ammunition that continues to empower armed gangs and destabilize the country.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports the US-led draft resolution extending the mandate of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission, which remains vital for supporting the Haitian National Police and restoring stability. We propose two modest additions to reinforce robust safeguards against sexual exploitation and abuse and to keep open Council consideration of sustainable financing and operational models for the mission. We look forward to voting in favor of this timely text.

To protect Council consensus and avoid a veto from permanent members, the draft highlights the urgent need for predictable financing and notes discussions on sustainability, while avoiding any premature operationalization of a UN peacekeeping transition mechanism.

messages.Algeria: Algeria thanks the co-penholders for constructively accommodating our proposals in the revised draft, particularly by recognizing CARICOM's commendable facilitation efforts and reinforcing the strict enforcement of the arms embargo. We fully support the renewal of the Multinational Security Support mission, under the commendable leadership of Kenya, and stand ready to vote in favour of the text as currently drafted.
messages.China: China appreciates the penholders' constructive approach and positive response to our concerns in Revision 1, particularly regarding the arms embargo, the emphasis on voluntary contributions, and the advancement of the political process. The current text strikes a balanced approach to supporting Haiti's security while respecting Haitian ownership and Council unity. China is prepared to support the draft resolution as currently formulated.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the co-penholders for constructively accommodating our proposals regarding human rights compliance, child protection, and robust mechanisms to prevent and respond to sexual exploitation and abuse. We fully support this balanced draft resolution extending the authorization of the Multinational Security Support mission to assist the Haitian National Police in restoring security and protecting civilians. Denmark stands ready to vote in favour of the resolution as drafted.
messages.France: France thanks the co-penholders for incorporating our proposals regarding linguistic capabilities in French and Haitian Creole, as well as cooperation with the International Organization of la Francophonie. The draft text effectively ensures the necessary extension and operational continuity of the MSS mission while maintaining strong emphasis on human rights compliance, arms embargo enforcement, and political progress. France is fully satisfied with the revised draft and stands ready to vote in favour.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the co-penholders, the United States and Panama, for incorporating our proposals regarding child protection and mechanisms to prevent and respond to sexual exploitation and abuse into operative paragraph 3. We fully support this balanced draft resolution renewing the authorization of the Multinational Security Support mission to bolster the Haitian National Police and protect civilians. Greece stands ready to vote in favour of the text as currently drafted.
messages.Guyana: Guyana expresses its sincere appreciation to the co-penholders for constructively accommodating our proposals in this revision, notably recognizing CARICOM's ongoing facilitation efforts and personnel contributions, as well as underscoring the necessity of predictable and sustainable support for the MSS mission. We believe this balanced text provides the requisite backing for the mission to assist the Haitian National Police and advance stability. Guyana is fully satisfied with the current text and stands ready to vote in favour.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks the co-penholders for constructively accommodating our suggestions regarding the illicit trafficking of arms and the urgent need for humanitarian assistance. The current text strikes a balanced approach in supporting the Multinational Security Support mission while reaffirming Haiti's sovereignty and the necessity of an inclusive, Haitian-led political process. Pakistan fully supports the adoption of the draft resolution in its current form.
messages.Panama: As co-sponsor and regional partner, Panama fully supports this draft resolution to extend the mandate of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission for an additional twelve months. The text strikes the necessary balance by ensuring operational continuity, emphasizing human rights compliance and child protection, and reaffirming the need for predictable resources alongside a Haitian-led political transition. We urge all Council members to support the adoption of this text without delay to send a unified signal of solidarity to the Haitian people.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea fully supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission. We commend the co-penholders for presenting a balanced text that addresses the critical need for sustainable and predictable financing, reinforces the operational capacity of the Haitian National Police, and underscores accountability and human rights compliance. We stand ready to vote in favour of the resolution as drafted.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation appreciates the penholders' constructive approach in accommodating our key proposals, particularly regarding the reinforcement of the arms embargo and maintaining the focus on the MSS mission's current mandate. As the revised text refrains from premature initiatives to alter the format of the international presence into a United Nations peacekeeping operation, we can support the draft as currently formulated. We reiterate that addressing the flow of illicit arms and advancing an inclusive Haitian-led political process remain indispensable to achieving lasting stability.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks the penholders for constructive engagement and for incorporating language addressing the acute funding shortfalls and the imperative of predictable and sustainable financing for the MSS mission. In solidarity with the Haitian people and in support of Kenya and participating CARICOM states, Sierra Leone fully supports the 12-month renewal of the mission's authorization. We look forward to voting in favour of this draft resolution.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the co-penholders for incorporating our suggestions regarding child protection, humanitarian access, and the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse into revision 1. The draft reflects a balanced approach addressing both operational security needs and fundamental human rights standards. We fully support the adoption of this text to ensure the uninterrupted authorization and sustained support for the MSS mission.
messages.Somalia: Somalia thanks the co-penholders for accommodating our proposals in this revision, particularly regarding predictable and sustainable financing for the MSS mission and the critical need to curb illicit arms flows. We strongly commend Kenya's leadership and the contributions of CARICOM and all troop-contributing countries to restoring peace and security in Haiti. Somalia fully supports the draft resolution as formulated and looks forward to voting in its favour.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom warmly thanks the United States and Panama for their leadership and for accommodating our proposals on sexual exploitation and abuse safeguards and sustainable financing. This draft resolution provides crucial continuity and mandate authority for the Multinational Security Support mission alongside the Haitian National Police. We fully support the text as drafted and stand ready to vote in favour.

steps.summary: All fifteen Council members expressed full support for the draft resolution without requesting further amendments. The draft maintains full consensus while extending the authorization of the Multinational Security Support mission for twelve months and reinforcing arms embargo enforcement, human rights compliance, and predictable funding.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria consistently supports international efforts to assist Haiti, particularly the African- and CARICOM-supported Multinational Security Support mission, in full respect of Haitian ownership and sovereignty.
reasons.China: China supports the extension of the Multinational Security Support mission's authorization to assist the Haitian National Police in curbing rampant gang violence, while consistently emphasizing the strict implementation of the arms embargo and the primacy of a Haitian-led political process.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark supports the extension of the Multinational Security Support mission to help stabilize Haiti and appreciates the inclusion of strong human rights, child protection, and accountability provisions.
reasons.France: France strongly supports extending the mandate of the Multinational Security Support mission to help stabilize Haiti and assist the Haitian National Police, particularly with the inclusion of language training and Francophonie cooperation in the text. As per standard French practice on this item, France will vote in favour and deliver its remarks after the adoption.
reasons.Greece: Greece supports the renewal of the MSS mission mandate to assist the Haitian National Police in curbing gang violence, protecting civilians, and restoring stability, fully aligning with our EU partners and consistent with our previous voting record.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana steadfastly supports the renewal of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission to assist the Haitian National Police and stabilize the security situation, aligned with CARICOM's priorities and its ongoing collaboration with the A3+ group. In accordance with its standard practice on this agenda item, Guyana will vote in favour and reserve its remarks for an explanation of vote after the adoption.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan consistently supports multilateral and UN-authorized efforts to restore peace and stability in Haiti, in line with its established voting record and full support expressed during negotiations. As there are no contentious issues requiring an explanation of vote before the vote, Pakistan casts its vote in favour without a prior statement.
reasons.Panama: As co-sponsor of the draft resolution and a regional partner committed to stabilizing Haiti, Panama strongly votes in favor of extending the MSS mission's mandate to reinforce the Haitian National Police and support the restoration of democratic institutions.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea firmly supports the renewal of the Multinational Security Support mission's mandate to assist the Haitian National Police in restoring security and creating conditions for an inclusive, Haitian-led political process. In line with standard practice on this file, Korea will cast an affirmative vote and reserves any remarks for after the vote.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia supports extending the mandate of the Multinational Security Support Mission in Haiti to assist the Haitian National Police in curbing gang violence, while maintaining its preference to deliver its formal explanation of vote after the adoption.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone consistently supports international security assistance for Haiti, specifically the renewal of the Kenya-led Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission, to help stabilize the security environment, protect civilians, and support the Haitian National Police.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia strongly supports extending the authorization of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission to assist the Haitian National Police in addressing rampant gang violence and restoring stability. The resolution adequately incorporates key priorities for Slovenia, including human rights compliance, child protection, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, and strictly enforcing the arms embargo.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia strongly supports the extension of the Multinational Security Support mission in Haiti, particularly given the leadership of fellow East African partner Kenya, and aligns with the Council's consensus to help restore stability and curb gang violence.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports extending the mandate of the Multinational Security Support mission in Haiti to assist the Haitian National Police and stabilize the country, aligning with our consistent voting record on this agenda item. In line with our standard practice on this file, we will deliver our statement after the vote.
reasons.United States of America: As the co-penholder and sponsor of the resolution renewing the MSS mission's mandate, the United States strongly supports the text and delivers an introductory statement urging unanimous adoption and sustained international funding.

before.Panama:
(spoke in Spanish)

Panama is proud to co-sponsor the draft resolution before us today alongside the United States. 

As a country of the region, Panama remains deeply committed to the stability, sovereignty, and democratic future of Haiti. The worsening security crisis, fueled by armed gang violence and illicit arms flows, continues to inflict tremendous suffering on the Haitian people. In this context, the renewal of the authorization for the Multinational Security Support mission is not merely a procedural necessity; it is a vital imperative to assist the Haitian National Police, restore public order, protect vulnerable civilian populations, and establish the conditions necessary to advance an inclusive, Haitian-led political process toward free, fair, and transparent elections.

We commend Kenya for its continued leadership of the mission, along with the contributions of our partners in CARICOM and the broader international community. At the same time, we emphasize that the mission requires predictable, adequate resources and sustained international solidarity. We urge all members of the Security Council to vote in favor of this resolution.
before.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The United States, together with our co-penholder Panama, is proud to put forward this draft resolution to extend the mandate of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission in Haiti for another twelve months. 

The people of Haiti continue to endure unimaginable suffering from rampant gang violence, grave human rights abuses, and severe humanitarian deprivation. In the face of these immense challenges, the MSS mission—operating side-by-side with the Haitian National Police—represents a crucial lifeline. We extend our profound gratitude to Kenya for its steadfast leadership, to Jamaica, the Bahamas, and other CARICOM partners for their vital personnel contributions, and to all Member States that have provided indispensable financial and logistical support.

While the deployment of the MSS mission has begun to assist the Haitian National Police in pushing back against gang terror, much more must be done. The mission urgently requires predictable, sustainable resources, specialized capabilities, and expanded personnel to achieve its full operational capacity. At the same time, security assistance must go hand in hand with political progress. We urge Haitian stakeholders to work collaboratively to advance an inclusive, credible political process that will restore democratic order and lead to free, fair, and transparent elections.

Today’s resolution sends an unmistakable message of Council unity and solidarity with the Haitian people. We call on all Council members to vote in favour of this draft resolution and to match their votes with concrete contributions to the MSS trust fund and to humanitarian assistance. 

Thank you, Mr. President.

after.Algeria:
Mr. President,

Algeria voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which extends the mandate of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission in Haiti for an additional period of twelve months.

Our positive vote reflects Algeria’s steadfast solidarity with the brotherly Haitian people in their arduous quest to overcome the multifaceted security, humanitarian, and political crisis that continues to afflict their nation. 

We wish to pay special tribute to the Government and people of Kenya for their courageous and exemplary leadership of the MSS mission. We also express our sincere appreciation to the member States of CARICOM and all other contributing countries that have stepped forward with personnel, logistical, and financial support. This deployment represents a noble demonstration of South-South cooperation and international solidarity in the face of immense adversity.

While the deployment of the MSS mission, in coordination with the Haitian National Police, remains an essential tool to counter criminal gangs, curb pervasive violence, and protect innocent civilians, Algeria wishes to reiterate three fundamental points:

First, security measures alone cannot resolve the crisis in Haiti. A lasting and sustainable solution can only emerge through an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process. We urge all Haitian political and civil society stakeholders to set aside narrow differences, transcend partisan divisions, and work constructively together toward the restoration of democratic institutions through credible, transparent, and peaceful elections.

Second, the international community must address the root drivers of instability, including poverty, institutional fragility, and the severe humanitarian catastrophe. We call on international donors to scale up their contributions to the UN Trust Fund and to expand humanitarian assistance to alleviate the suffering of the Haitian people. Furthermore, as we look to the future, the provision of predictable, adequate, and sustainable financing for international security assistance remains indispensable.

Third, we emphasize the paramount importance of strictly implementing and enforcing the targeted arms embargo established by this Council. Armed gangs cannot sustain their terror without the continuous influx of illicit weapons and ammunition originating from abroad. Member States, particularly in the region, must redouble their efforts and take stringent, decisive measures to halt the illicit trafficking and diversion of arms to non-State armed groups in Haiti.

In conclusion, Mr. President, Algeria reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity of Haiti. We remain fully dedicated to supporting the Haitian people on their path toward enduring peace, stability, and development.

I thank you.
after.China:
(spoke in Chinese):

China voted in favour of the resolution just adopted extending the authorization of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission in Haiti.

At present, the security and humanitarian situation in Haiti remains grave. Gang violence continues to plague the country, threatening the lives and property of the Haitian people and destabilizing the wider region. In this context, extending the authorization of the MSS mission is necessary to assist the Haitian National Police in curbing gang violence and restoring public order. We commend Kenya, CARICOM countries, and other contributors for their leadership, commitment, and valuable contributions to the mission.

At the same time, China wishes to emphasize the following points:

First, external security assistance is only a means to buy time and space; it cannot replace the efforts of the Haitian people themselves. The root causes of the crisis in Haiti are political and institutional. The only viable path forward is an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process. We urge the Transitional Presidential Council and all political forces and factions in Haiti to place the interests of the country and its people first, overcome differences, advance dialogue in good faith, and urgently establish a credible and clear roadmap for holding free, fair, and transparent elections as soon as security conditions permit, so as to restore constitutional order.

Second, stemming the illicit flow of weapons and ammunition is critical to resolving the security crisis. Gang violence in Haiti is directly sustained by weapons and ammunition trafficked from abroad. The Security Council has repeatedly strengthened the targeted arms embargo on Haiti. However, illicit arms continue to flow into the hands of criminal gangs. We call on all countries, especially those from which weapons and ammunition originate or through which they transit, to take concrete and effective measures to strictly enforce the Council's arms embargo, tighten export controls, and effectively sever the supply chains that arm criminal networks in Haiti.

Third, the MSS mission must continue to enhance its operational effectiveness and coordination with the Haitian National Police. Adequate attention must be paid to human rights compliance, the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, and strict adherence to international law. Any long-term security arrangement must fully respect Haiti's sovereignty, take into account past lessons learned from international involvement in the country, and be approached with prudence and broad consensus.

China stands ready to work with members of the Security Council and the international community to continue supporting the Haitian people in overcoming their present difficulties and achieving lasting peace, stability, and development.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Denmark:
Thank you, Mr. President.

Denmark welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution extending the authorization of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission in Haiti. We thank the co-penholders, the United States and Panama, for their diligent efforts in steering this Council toward consensus.

The situation in Haiti remains deeply alarming. Millions of Haitians continue to face unacceptable levels of gang violence, severe food insecurity, and widespread violations and abuses of human rights. We are particularly horrified by the systematic use of sexual and gender-based violence by armed gangs and the alarming recruitment and exploitation of children. 

Denmark commends Kenya for its continued leadership of the MSS mission, as well as the personnel contributions from Jamaica, the Bahamas, and other partners, alongside CARICOM’s tireless engagement. Their presence alongside the Haitian National Police provides an indispensable foundation for restoring security and protecting civilians. 

For Denmark, it is of paramount importance that the MSS mission operates in full compliance with international law, including international human rights law, and that robust accountability mechanisms are upheld, particularly regarding the prevention of and response to sexual exploitation and abuse, as well as child protection. 

At the same time, security operations alone cannot resolve Haiti's multidimensional crisis. Sustainable stability requires an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political dialogue that establishes a credible path toward democratic institutions through free, fair, and transparent elections. Furthermore, we urge all Member States to strictly enforce the targeted sanctions regime and arms embargo to stem the illicit flow of weapons and ammunition fueling the violence. 

Finally, the MSS mission urgently needs predictable, sustainable, and flexible funding and resources. Denmark calls on the international community to step up its voluntary contributions to the UN Trust Fund and to provide vital humanitarian assistance to relieve the acute suffering of the Haitian people.

Thank you.
after.France:
(spoke in French):

France welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution renewing the authorization of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission in Haiti for a period of twelve months. We thank the United States and Panama for their dedicated work as co-penholders.

The security and humanitarian situation in Haiti remains deeply alarming. Armed gangs continue to terrorize the civilian population, commit appalling acts of violence, and severely restrict humanitarian access. In this critical context, the continued presence and operational ramp-up of the MSS mission, operating alongside the Haitian National Police, is indispensable to restoring public order, protecting civilians, and creating the necessary security conditions for the holding of free, fair, and democratic elections.

France commends Kenya for its continued leadership and courage at the helm of the mission, and we express our deep appreciation to the member States of CARICOM and other international partners who have deployed personnel or provided vital logistical and financial support.

For its part, France has consistently mobilized to support security in Haiti. We were among the very first contributors to the United Nations Trust Fund for the MSS mission, and we have provided substantial bilateral assistance to equip and train the Haitian National Police. Through our cooperation with the International Organization of la Francophonie, France has also funded French and Haitian Creole language training to ensure smooth coordination between deployed personnel and the Haitian population. On the humanitarian front, France continues to provide crucial assistance to the most vulnerable.

However, the international community must be lucid: the MSS mission cannot succeed without predictable, sustainable, and sufficient resources. We must address the persistent funding shortfalls and seriously consider all viable options, including the recommendations put forward by the Secretary-General, to ensure the long-term sustainability of international security assistance to Haiti.

At the same time, we must stem the flow of weapons that fuels gang violence. The strict implementation and enforcement of the arms embargo established by this Council is an absolute priority. 

Finally, security support cannot substitute for political progress. France calls on all Haitian political and civil society actors to put narrow interests aside and urgently advance an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political transition to restore democratic institutions. France will continue to stand firmly by the side of the Haitian people on their path toward peace, justice, and stability.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Greece:
Mr. President,

Greece welcomed the unanimous adoption of resolution 2793 (2025), extending the authorization of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission in Haiti for another twelve months. Our vote in favour reflects our steadfast commitment to the principles of the United Nations Charter, international solidarity, and our deep concern for the enduring plight of the Haitian people.

The security, humanitarian, and human rights situation in Haiti remains alarming. Armed gangs continue to perpetrate grave atrocities, including rampant sexual and gender-based violence, kidnappings, and the egregious recruitment and use of children. In this context, the MSS mission, operating in close coordination with the Haitian National Police, remains an indispensable tool to help restore public order, secure critical infrastructure, and protect civilians.

We express our sincere appreciation to the Government of Kenya for its steadfast leadership of the mission, as well as to Jamaica, the Bahamas, and other CARICOM partners, and all contributing States, for their courage and dedication on the ground. We also commend the co-penholders, the United States and Panama, for their diligent efforts in guiding this resolution to a consensus.

For the MSS mission to fully deliver on its mandate, predictable, sustainable, and flexible funding is essential. We echo the call for the international community to scale up voluntary financial, logistical, and material support through the UN Trust Fund. Concurrently, it is paramount that all operations strictly adhere to international human rights law and international humanitarian law, with robust accountability and prevention mechanisms against sexual exploitation and abuse, as well as dedicated child protection measures.

Furthermore, we reiterate that security measures alone cannot resolve the crisis. The strict enforcement of the targeted sanctions regime, particularly the arms embargo, is vital to stemming the illicit flow of weapons and ammunition that fuel gang violence. Above all, a lasting solution must be Haitian-owned and Haitian-led. We urge all political actors in Haiti to set aside narrow interests, engage in constructive and inclusive dialogue, and advance a credible roadmap leading to the restoration of democratic institutions through free, fair, and transparent elections as soon as security conditions allow.

Greece stands in full solidarity with the people of Haiti in their pursuit of peace, stability, and dignity.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Guyana:
I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the three African members of the Security Council, namely Algeria, Sierra Leone, and Somalia, as well as my own country, Guyana (A3+).

The A3+ welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission for an additional twelve months. We express our appreciation to the co-penholders, Panama and the United States, for their leadership and collaborative approach throughout the negotiation process to achieve consensus.

Our vote in favour of this resolution reflects our steadfast commitment to the people of Haiti and our support for international efforts to assist Haitian authorities in restoring peace, security, and stability. We commend the continued leadership of Kenya, as well as the personnel contributions and support from CARICOM member States and other international partners who are operating alongside the Haitian National Police (HNP) under extremely perilous conditions.

While the MSS mission has made important strides in supporting the HNP to secure critical infrastructure and confront criminal gangs, the security and humanitarian situations on the ground remain deeply alarming. Armed gangs continue to perpetrate heinous acts of violence, including killings, kidnappings, sexual and gender-based violence, and the recruitment of children, while hundreds of thousands of Haitians remain internally displaced. 

In this context, we emphasize that the MSS mission must be provided with the necessary resources, equipment, and logistical backing to achieve full operational capability. The funding shortfalls currently facing the mission are of serious concern. We urge the international community and Member States to urgently scale up predictable and sustainable financial and material support, including through the United Nations Trust Fund, to ensure the mission can fulfill its mandate effectively.

The A3+ also reiterates that security assistance alone cannot solve the multidimensional crisis facing Haiti. We call for the strict implementation and enforcement of the targeted sanctions and the comprehensive arms embargo. Stemming the illicit flow and trafficking of weapons and ammunition into Haiti is vital to disabling the criminal gangs and preventing further bloodshed. 

Finally, we stress that sustainable peace can only be achieved through a truly inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process. We urge all Haitian stakeholders to work together in good faith to advance the political transition and establish a clear, credible path toward holding free, fair, and transparent democratic elections. CARICOM remains actively engaged in facilitating political dialogue, and the A3+ reaffirms its unwavering solidarity with the Haitian people as they strive to reclaim their security, dignity, and democratic future.

I thank you.
after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, extending the authorization of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission in Haiti for an additional twelve months. 

Our vote reflects Pakistan’s longstanding solidarity with the people of Haiti and our steadfast commitment to collective international efforts aimed at restoring security, stability, and democratic governance in the country. Pakistan has a proud history of contributing to United Nations peace operations in Haiti, and we remain deeply invested in its peaceful and prosperous future.

The multidimensional crisis facing Haiti remains deeply alarming. Rampant gang violence, horrific human rights abuses, acute food insecurity, and the widespread displacement of innocent civilians demand our urgent, sustained, and coordinated attention. In this regard, the deployment of the MSS mission, operating in support of the Haitian National Police, remains a vital instrument to assist Haitian authorities in reclaiming public safety and protecting vulnerable populations. 

We express our deep appreciation to Kenya for its commendable leadership of the MSS mission, as well as to the member States of the Caribbean Community (CARICOM) and other international partners that have contributed personnel, resources, and vital logistical support under exceptionally difficult circumstances. 

At the same time, we must recognize that the mission faces severe resource constraints. To ensure its full operational effectiveness and long-term viability, the international community must step forward with predictable, flexible, and sustainable financial, logistical, and technical contributions, including through the UN Trust Fund. 

Security measures alone, however, cannot resolve Haiti’s complex challenges. A lasting solution can only be achieved through an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political dialogue that establishes a credible roadmap toward the restoration of democratic institutions and the holding of free, fair, and transparent elections. We welcome the constructive engagement and facilitation efforts of CARICOM in this regard.

Furthermore, it is imperative to address the illicit flow of arms and ammunition that continues to empower criminal gangs and destabilize the country. We urge all Member States to strictly enforce the targeted arms embargo established by this Council to stem these illicit flows at their source.

In conclusion, Mr. President, Pakistan reiterates its unwavering support for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and unity of Haiti, and we stand ready to continue working constructively with all Council members and international partners to help the Haitian people achieve enduring peace and stability.

I thank you.
after.Republic of Korea:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The Republic of Korea voted in favour of the resolution extending the mandate of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission in Haiti. We thank the co-penholders, the United States and Panama, for their diligent efforts in steering this resolution to a unanimous adoption.

The multidimensional crisis in Haiti continues to inflict immense suffering on its people. Rampant gang violence, severe human rights violations, including sexual and gender-based violence and the recruitment of children, and mass displacement demand the sustained attention and decisive support of the international community. 

In this context, the MSS mission plays an indispensable role in supporting the Haitian National Police to restore public order, protect critical infrastructure, and build the security conditions necessary for lasting peace. We express our deep appreciation to Kenya for its steadfast leadership of the mission, as well as to Jamaica, the Bahamas, and other CARICOM partners and contributing States for their vital contributions on the ground.

At the same time, we must recognize that the mission’s success hinges on adequate, predictable, and sustainable resources. Funding shortfalls and logistical deficits hinder the mission’s full operational capability. The Republic of Korea once again urges the international community to step forward with voluntary financial, logistical, and material support, including through the UN Trust Fund. We also stand ready to continue our engagement in discussions on options to ensure long-term and sustainable security assistance to Haiti.

Furthermore, restoring stability requires cutting off the supply of illicit weapons that empower armed gangs. We call on all Member States to strictly enforce the UN arms embargo and take robust measures to stem the illicit flow of arms and ammunition into Haiti.

Ultimately, security assistance alone cannot resolve Haiti’s crisis. Peace and stability can only take root through a truly inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process. We urge all Haitian political stakeholders to put aside differences, advance national dialogue, and establish a clear roadmap toward the holding of free, fair, and democratic elections.

The Republic of Korea reaffirms its enduring solidarity with the people of Haiti and will continue to work constructively with Council members and international partners to support Haiti on its path to peace, stability, and development.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the United States and Panama extending the mandate of the Multinational Security Support Mission in Haiti for another year.

Our support for the resolution is guided by our principled stance in favour of assisting the long-suffering Haitian people in overcoming the profound security crisis that has engulfed their country. We once again express our appreciation to Kenya, the participating States of the Caribbean Community, and other personnel-contributing countries for their efforts and dedication in seeking to stabilize the security environment in Haiti under extremely complex and dangerous conditions.

At the same time, we must reiterate our conviction that force alone cannot resolve the crisis in Haiti. The security challenges facing the country are intimately tied to deep-seated socio-economic deprivation and the ongoing institutional breakdown. Crucially, armed violence is sustained by the relentless influx of illicit weapons and ammunition. As we have repeatedly stressed, the vast majority of these arms originate in the United States and are smuggled into Haiti to arm the criminal gangs terrorizing the population. We call on all States, particularly those from whose territory these weapons flow, to take real, effective, and verifiable measures to strictly enforce the Council’s arms embargo. Without cutting off the illicit supply of weapons, no security mission will be able to achieve sustainable success.

Furthermore, we continue to believe that any discussions regarding altering the modalities of the international presence, including any premature proposals to transform the Mission into a United Nations peacekeeping operation, must be approached with extreme caution, taking into full account the complex and unfortunate historical track record of UN peacekeeping in Haiti. The priority must remain the proper equipping, training, and operational support of the Haitian National Police, which must ultimately assume full responsibility for maintaining law and order.

Finally, a durable solution can only be achieved through a truly inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political dialogue. External actors must refrain from imposing political formulas from the outside. Only by restoring legitimate constitutional institutions and organizing credible democratic elections can Haiti pave a path toward long-term peace and stability.
after.Sierra Leone:
Mr. President,

I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the members of the A3+, namely Algeria, Guyana, Somalia, and my own country, Sierra Leone.

We welcome the unanimous adoption of the resolution just adopted, extending the authorization of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission in Haiti for an additional period of twelve months. We express our appreciation to the co-penholders, the United States and Panama, for their collaborative approach throughout the negotiation process.

The unanimous renewal of this mandate sends a clear, unified, and resolute message of the Security Council’s continued commitment to stand in solidarity with the people of Haiti as they confront profound security, humanitarian, and political challenges. 

The A3+ pays special tribute to the Government and people of Kenya for their steadfast leadership and courage in deploying and leading the MSS mission on the ground in Port-au-Prince. We also warmly commend the personnel and Governments of CARICOM member states—notably Jamaica, the Bahamas, and Belize—as well as other contributing nations, who have demonstrated historic pan-African and regional solidarity by contributing troops, police, and vital resources to assist the Haitian National Police in reclaiming public safety and restoring state authority.

While the deployment of the MSS mission represents a critical step forward, the mission continues to face severe operational, logistical, and financial constraints. We reiterate our strong call on the international community and bilateral partners to match their commitments with tangible, flexible, predictable, and sustained financial contributions, including through the United Nations Trust Fund. The security of Haiti cannot be sustained on temporary pledges alone; adequate and reliable funding is essential to enable the mission to achieve its full operational capacity and effectively assist the Haitian National Police in neutralizing criminal gang networks.

Security measures alone, however, will not resolve the multidimensional crisis in Haiti. A sustainable solution requires addressing the root causes of instability. The A3+ emphasizes that lasting peace can only be achieved through an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process. We urge the Transitional Presidential Council and all Haitian political and civil society stakeholders to put aside narrow interests, preserve national cohesion, and urgently advance the political roadmap aimed at restoring democratic institutions and holding free, fair, and credible elections as soon as security conditions permit.

Furthermore, we underscore the indispensable necessity of strictly enforcing the targeted sanctions and the comprehensive arms embargo. The relentless illicit flow of firearms and ammunition into Haiti fuels the lethal violence perpetrated by armed gangs. All Member States must take concrete, robust measures to prevent and intercept the illicit trafficking and diversion of arms and ammunition to non-state armed groups in Haiti.

In conclusion, the A3+ reaffirms its unwavering solidarity with the resilient people of Haiti in their quest for peace, stability, justice, and socio-economic development. We remain fully committed to supporting all collective efforts aimed at securing a peaceful and prosperous future for Haiti.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Slovenia:
Thank you, Mr. President.

Slovenia voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which extends the authorization of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission in Haiti for an additional twelve months. 

We commend the co-penholders, Panama and the United States, for their efforts in steering this process to a unanimous outcome, which sends a clear and unified signal of the Security Council’s continued solidarity with the people of Haiti. We also express our sincere appreciation to Kenya for its leadership of the mission, as well as to Jamaica, the Bahamas, and other CARICOM and international partners who have contributed personnel and resources under challenging conditions.

The multifaceted crisis in Haiti remains alarming. The relentless violence perpetrated by armed gangs continues to inflict immense suffering on the civilian population, driving displacement, exacerbating acute food insecurity, and severely restricting humanitarian access. Slovenia is particularly appalled by the pervasive sexual and gender-based violence used as a tactic of terror, as well as the grave violations committed against children, notably their recruitment and exploitation by criminal gangs.

While the deployment of the MSS mission alongside the Haitian National Police is essential to restoring public order and protecting civilians, military and police measures alone cannot solve this crisis. We reiterate that:

First, all operations conducted by the MSS mission and the Haitian National Police must strictly adhere to international law, including international human rights law and international humanitarian law. Robust oversight, child protection frameworks, and zero-tolerance mechanisms against sexual exploitation and abuse must be fully integrated and rigorously enforced.

Second, the mission urgently requires predictable, sustainable, and adequate financing. We call upon the international community to step up voluntary contributions to the UN Trust Fund and provide the necessary logistical and operational support.

Third, stemming the illicit flow of weapons and ammunition into Haiti is vital. We call for the strict implementation and enforcement of the Council’s arms embargo, as armed gangs cannot sustain their terror without illicit weapons trafficking.

Finally, long-term stability can only be achieved through an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process. We urge all Haitian political and civil society actors to work together in good faith to advance the transitional roadmap and create the necessary security and political conditions for holding free, fair, and transparent democratic elections.

Slovenia remains firmly committed to supporting Haiti and its people on the path toward peace, security, rule of law, and democratic governance.

Thank you.
after.Somalia:
Mr. President,

after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution extending the authorization of the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission for a further twelve months. We thank the co-penholders, the United States and Panama, for their leadership and dedication throughout these negotiations.

The unanimous vote today demonstrates the Security Council’s continued and resolute commitment to supporting the people of Haiti as they face severe insecurity, grave humanitarian distress, and pervasive gang violence.

Finally, we reiterate our call for the strict implementation and enforcement of the arms embargo. Stemming the illicit flow of weapons and ammunition into Haiti is vital to breaking the grip of armed gangs.

Thank you.
